answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 23 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the atlas solution is checked at the lagoon gate and logged, the walnut audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
